# SSMConnect

> SSMConnect is a free, open-source app for Windows and Linux. Its flagship feature is copying files between AWS servers with two panes and a Copy button through AWS Systems Manager, so inbound port 22 stays closed. It also finds EC2 servers, opens SSH and Remote Desktop connections over Session Manager and sets up PuTTY, WinSCP and MobaXterm.

For the full list of pages in Markdown, see https://poonchezhian.github.io/sitemap.md.

## Start here

- [Home](https://poonchezhian.github.io/index.md): what it does, how it works, requirements, safety and FAQ
- [Copy files between servers](https://poonchezhian.github.io/file-transfer/index.md): the two-pane file window, how the data travels, limits
- [Documentation](https://poonchezhian.github.io/docs/index.md): setup, dashboard, accounts, troubleshooting, security, Linux
- [Blog](https://poonchezhian.github.io/blog/index.md): articles and release notes

## Blog

- [How to copy files between EC2 servers when port 22 is closed](https://poonchezhian.github.io/blog/copy-files-between-ec2-servers-port-22-closed/index.md): Four ways to move files from one EC2 server to another when SSH is closed and you only have AWS Systems Manager: S3, manual port forwarding, rsync, and a two-pane window in SSMConnect.
- [What is new in SSMConnect 2.0: connections that stay open and a calmer dashboard](https://poonchezhian.github.io/blog/ssmconnect-2-0-whats-new/index.md): A tour of SSMConnect 2.0 to 2.0.5 for Windows: connect-all with keep-alive, login checks before PuTTY opens, usage bars, a file window that matches the dashboard, and a scrolling grid for large fleets.
- [Is it safe to copy files between servers through your PC?](https://poonchezhian.github.io/blog/is-it-safe-to-copy-files-through-your-pc/index.md): How SSMConnect's file transfer is built: SSH inside the SSM tunnel, streaming through memory, no root, a private sudo helper, and the limits you should know about.
- [SSM port forwarding explained for developers](https://poonchezhian.github.io/blog/ssm-port-forwarding-explained/index.md): What AWS Systems Manager port forwarding does, why your tools connect to 127.0.0.1, and how one tunnel per server lets PuTTY, WinSCP and Remote Desktop work with no open ports.
